ballots.name: Priya
ballots.reason: With caching bringing runtime to sub-minute parallel, baseline mode silencing legacy noise, and a two-week report-only pilot before enforcement, every cost concern I raised in round one is resolved and the conditions converge into a rollout I can defend.

ballots.name: Marcus
ballots.reason: With the job running parallel, cached, baseline-mode on changed lines only, no cascade reruns, and a two-week instrumented pilot on our actual monorepo, my queue arithmetic holds and I sign off on adoption.

ballots.name: Elena
ballots.reason: Lintwise's secret rules would have caught last quarter's hard-coded key in seconds as a parallel job, and with the team's agreed conditions—complementing not replacing our SCA and secret-scan steps, and assigning a quarterly dependency-update owner—this is a clear net security win with minimal queue impact.

ballots.name: Tom
ballots.reason: Baseline mode silences the legacy-JS noise that would otherwise flood every PR, Jin and I will co-own the rule-set tuning so enforcement targets real defects rather than formatter trivia, and the two-week report-only pilot with Marcus's instrumentation gives me the runtime number I need before the gate goes hard.

ballots.name: Sana
ballots.reason: Baseline mode silences existing SQL and Jinja patterns by only checking changed lines, the pilot is scoped to my data subdirectories, and the eight-percent FP ceiling with rollback gives me a hard trigger if dialect-specific false positives still leak through—so my round-one fear of suppression-comment sprawl is now bounded and testable before enforcement.

ballots.name: Lars
ballots.reason: Baseline mode plus the eight-percent FP ceiling, enforced through a two-week report-only pilot with no cascade reruns, gives me the signal-to-noise gate I need so that every new violation blocking a merge is a real defect and not legacy noise—exactly the test-signal hygiene I've been arguing for since round one.

ballots.name: Jin
ballots.reason: With parallel cached execution, baseline mode scoping enforcement to changed lines, an eight-percent FP rollback ceiling, no-cascade-rerun policy, one-rule-at-a-time promotion, and a two-week report-only pilot on our actual monorepo, the conditions I set as merge-policy owner are fully met and every colleague's concern is addressed—this is a guardrail, not a ceremony.

ballots.name: Olga
ballots.reason: With baseline mode scoping checks to changed lines only, the parallel sub-minute cached job, and Jin owning a visible two-week pilot with an eight-percent false-positive rollback trigger, Lintwise becomes the clear, low-friction style guide I need to stop guessing house conventions without adding CI minutes or legacy-file noise to my PRs.
